risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: sql/audit_checkpoint_schema.sql CHECK-constrained audit_table to three names while api/_lib/audit.js carried sixteen audit logs, so 13 of 16 logs could never be checkpointed and the daily job reported ok over 19% of the population -- a pass it never performed on the other thirteen. And the file could not fix itself: `create table if not exists` skips an existing table constraint and all, so re-running it to widen coverage would have reported success and changed nothing. Fixed by making the file one idempotent block (create-with-sixteen PLUS a drop-constraint-if-exists/add-constraint pair that acts on an already-created table), deriving SCHEMA_PERMITTED from AUDIT_TABLE_BY_APP instead of a second hand-kept list, and adding a 503 CHECK_NOT_WIDENED refusal so an unrun migration is named rather than falling through to a generic 502 advising a retry that can never work.

risks.risk: api/_lib/deadline-engine.js applyRetrigger(): one filter, `!toUTC(e.disposition_date)`, decided whether a qualifying post-judgment motion was still pending. toUTC returns null for anything that is not strictly YYYY-MM-DD, so a caller sending `12/31/2026`, `Dec 31 2026`, `2026-13-45` or a misspelled key was reported as having an UNDISPOSED motion -- and api/legal-deadlines.js maps that MOTION_PENDING refusal to 422, so the reply read as a considered legal answer rather than as a parse failure: "the period runs from the disposition of the last such motion, so it has not started yet". On a motion that had been disposed. THE DIRECTION THAT LOSES THE APPEAL: a litigator told the appeal clock has not begun, in a message specific enough to be believed, when it began at the disposition weeks earlier. FRAP 4(a)(4)(A) and its analogues are the rules in question and all three are SEEDED and live (two US federal rules, Ohio App.R. 4(B)(2), Massachusetts Rule 12(a)(2)). Fixed to three states keyed on WHAT THE CALLER SENT rather than on what it parsed to: absent, null or blank is genuinely PENDING and unchanged; a value present and unreadable is a new BAD_DISPOSITION_DATE naming the offending value and the one accepted format and saying in the message that it is not the same answer as pending; a readable date governs. A non-object element is also refused -- retrigger_events is caller-supplied, so `["rule_50b_motion"]` previously read as a pending motion. BAD_DISPOSITION_DATE is deliberately NOT in the 422 list and is NAMED on the 400 side so the mapping is a recorded decision. SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME FUNCTION, found by the suite written for the first: toUTC accepted `2026-02-30`, which passes the shape regex and which `new Date` does not reject -- it ROLLS OVER to 2026-03-02 and isNaN is false. Every date this engine takes (trigger dates, holiday rows, dispositions) accepted an impossible day and computed from a different one with no error. toUTC now calls api/_lib/calendar-date.js's isCalendarDate, which exists for exactly this, rather than growing an eighth hand-rolled date guard.

risks.risk: api/legal-citator.js feedback recorded no employee against a legal-citation treatment confirm or correction, at the application layer AND in sql/sairnlaw_citator_schema.sql, while that schema's own comment three lines above cl_feedback_log said 'individual feedback stays attributable'. logRec at :380 was built in the same function as auditLookup() at :185 from the same caller resolved at :184 and simply omitted it; the table had no employee column of any kind. Every row was attributable to a FIRM and to nobody, so an attorney confirming a classification other attorneys rely on was unrecoverable -- never captured rather than wrong. Fixed at both layers with NULLABLE columns on purpose, because the session token on this endpoint is optional by design and a row can legitimately have no person on it; inventing the owner or the licence would have read as evidence. The alter-table half is handled with a 503 NOT_PROVISIONED naming the SQL file, because create-table-if-not-exists does nothing to a live table and the old handler would have reported PGRST204 as 'try again'.

risks.risk: SAIRNlaw had exactly ONE role check across its whole data surface -- LAW_RECONCILE_ROLES, owner-only, on law_trust_reconcile -- and the other 19 law_ resources were session-gated with no role distinction, so any signed-in role could read and write law_picases (settlement figures, Tier A/A), law_pimedical (health information held by a law firm, Tier A/A) and law_bankstatements (the bank side of an IOLTA three-way reconciliation) exactly as freely as a managing attorney. Fixed with ONE data table and ONE function in api/_lib/law-roles.js, called from the TWO gates that already existed rather than nineteen per-resource ifs -- the defect being that a role check at one call site and not the others is indistinguishable from no policy when read one branch at a time. Three verdicts, not two: NOT_LAW keeps the law table from approving or refusing another app's resource in a block 70 action-pairs pass through. Trust resources are hard-locked in a SEPARATE structure consulted after the table agrees, so the lock survives a table edit or an override layer. Fails closed on an unlisted law_ resource, an undeclared role, a missing role and any verb that is not read. THE POLICY IS MICHAEL'S AND IS TRANSCRIBED, NOT DERIVED: api/sd-data.js declined to invent it twice in writing and the auditor routed without prescribing a fix.
